section: Further out, on a fast line
purpose: PHASE 1 of the outer-London pass: which outer stations are genuinely easy to get into central London from, before any hotel is looked at. Rob's rule (data/topics/hotels-budget.json openVenueQuestions, 14 Sep 2026): a direct Tube, Elizabeth line, DLR or Overground train to central London in about 30 minutes, with no change. Phase 2 drills into the top areas for budget hotel sources and records each hotel's own nearest station and walk.

rule.qualifies: A direct, no-change train from the station reaches ANY West End hub or ANY City hub in 30 minutes or less, on a service that also runs off-peak. 31-33 minutes is 'borderline' (the rule says 'about 30'); over 33, or no all-day direct service, is false.
rule.whyHubs: Coordinator's fix, 14 Sep 2026: Oxford Circus and Bank alone cannot be the destinations, because neither the Elizabeth line nor the Jubilee line - the two lines Rob wants prioritised - calls at either.
rule.monument: Monument counts as Bank: TfL runs Bank and Monument as one interchange, and it is where the District and Circle lines serve it. Rows where this decides the City figure say so in notes.
rule.peakOnly: A direct service with trains at 08:00-08:59 but none at 11:00-11:59 in TfL's timetable is listed under directOptions with peakOnly: true and is not used for the ranking or qualification. The case that prompted it: since the Battersea extension most Morden-branch Northern line trains run via Bank, so Clapham North to Leicester Square is 4 trains in the morning peak and none late morning.
rule.linesCounted: Tube, Elizabeth line, DLR and London Overground only. National Rail (Thameslink, Southeastern, c2c, Greater Anglia, South Western) is not counted, per the rule.

method.directServices: TfL Line Route Sequence API (Regular service type): a station and a hub are directly linked when both sit on one of the line's ordered routes. For each line the nearest West End hub and City hub by stop count (plus any within two further stops) were measured.
method.minutes: TfL Journey Planner API, departing 22/09/2026 (a Tuesday) at 08:30, journeyPreference=leastinterchange, mode restricted to the line's own mode. A journey is direct only if it has exactly one non-walking leg and no more than 2 minutes of walking. 'minutes' is that leg's duration - time on the train, platform to platform - the fastest of the direct departures returned. Walking from a hotel to the station is NOT included; Phase 2 records it per hotel.
method.frequency: peakTrainsPerHour counts trains leaving the station 08:00-08:59 on a weekday that reach the hub with no change; offPeakTrainsPerHour the same for 11:00-11:59. Tube and DLR: TfL Line Timetable API (Monday-Thursday schedule), counting only trains whose stopping pattern includes the hub. Elizabeth line and Overground: TfL has no timetable endpoint for these modes, so the Journey Planner was chained across 08:00-08:59 and the distinct direct departures counted - an approximation, and no off-peak figure. peakTrainsPerHourWithin2MinOfFastest sums, across distinct lines, the peak trains that reach a hub within 2 minutes of the fastest time - so Stratford is credited with both the Elizabeth line and the Central line to Liverpool Street.
method.night: nightServiceToAHub lists lines with a Friday/Saturday night service (TfL 'Night' service type) from the station to at least one hub. The Elizabeth line, DLR and the Weaver Overground have no night service.
method.zone: TfL's own stop data (route sequence API).
method.ranking: Qualifying stations first, then fastest all-day direct minutes to any hub, then peakTrainsPerHourWithin2MinOfFastest.
method.requests: 921 TfL API requests, throttled to one every 1.5 seconds, no API key, no contact details in any header. Responses cached in the session scratchpad.

caveats: These are the station's figures, not a hotel's. A hotel ten minutes' walk away is ten minutes slower; Phase 2 records each hotel's nearest station and walk.
One planned date and time. Engineering works or a timetable change can move a figure by a minute or two; anything the planner disagreed with the route data about is in notes, not hidden.

The station list is a hand-built selection of roughly zone 2-4 stations on the fast corridors - the Elizabeth line and Jubilee line complete for their zone 2-4 London stations, other lines selectively - not every station in London. Most of them qualify because they were chosen from the fast corridors; the table's use is the ORDER.
Ease here is train time and frequency only. It says nothing about whether an area has hotels, or budget ones - see data/reference/hotel-corpus.md and the sheet-is-not-the-market rule.

candidateHotels.rule: Outer hotels named by 2+ independent sources (distinct domains) in data/evidence.json byTopic['hotels-budget'] after the outer pass, plus every outer hotel on the main rate-sampled shortlist. Hostels, aparthotels, capsules/pods and university rooms are signposted, not ranked (Rob, 14 Sep 2026) - listed separately under signpostFormats. 'Outer' means outside the central where-to-stay areas: Earl's Court, West Brompton, Camden and Kennington count as outer here, per the pass brief; Bermondsey Square Hotel and The Tower Hotel were left with the central list.
candidateHotels.journeyMethod: Each hotel located through OpenStreetMap Nominatim (or its operator page where OSM had no record). TfL StopPoint search lists Tube, Elizabeth line, DLR and Overground stations within 1.6 km; TfL Journey Planner gives the walk (mode=walking) to the three nearest; each station's direct trains come from the Phase 1 method. 'nearestStation' is the shortest walk; 'bestDirectStation' appears when a different station gives the quickest walk plus train to a hub.
candidateHotels.verdictRule: The rule is about the TRAIN: a direct, no-change train to any West End or City hub in about 30 minutes. The walk is recorded separately and never folded into that test. A walk over 15 minutes is flagged rather than failed - that call is Rob's.
